claims.text: What the image looks like Bird's beak @ LES w prox dilate → achalasia
claims.quote: Bird's beak at LES with proximal dilation → achalasia

claims.text: Buzzword: bird's beak on barium swallow → achalasia
claims.quote: Bird's beak Barium swallow Achalasia

claims.text: Ex barium swallow: prox esophageal dilatation and incomplete LES relaxation, w inhomogeneous material in the dilated esophagus from undigested food; in severe achalasia, only sm quantities of contrast pass thru a beaklike esophagogastric junction
claims.quote: This image shows achalasia with proximal esophageal dilatation and incomplete lower esophageal sphincter relaxation. Note the inhomogeneous appearance of the material within the dilated esophagus due to undigested food that did not pass into the stomach (long arrows). In severe achalasia, only small quantities of contrast medium are able to pass through a beaklike esophagogastric junction (short arrows).
claims.locator: Barium Swallow Showing Dilated Esophagus image caption

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Barium swallow may show absence of progress peristaltic contractions during swallowing; typically the esophagus = dilated, often enormously, but = narrowed and beaklike @ the LES
claims.quote: Barium swallow may show absence of progressive peristaltic contractions during swallowing. Typically, the esophagus is dilated, often enormously, but is narrowed and beaklike at the LES.

claims.text: Barium swallow = a complementary test, often done in the initial phase when the cause of dysphagia = unknown, b/c manometry = more invasive
claims.quote: Barium swallow is a complementary test that is often performed during the initial phase of testing when the cause of dysphagia is unknown because manometry is more invasive.

claims.text: Barium swallow technique (her chart): use water-soluble contrast (Gastrografin) if perf sus; barium → peritonitis
claims.quote: Use water-soluble contrast (Gastrografin) if perforation suspected; barium causes peritonitis

claims.text: Sus perf = the main contraindication to radiographic contrast studies: free barium = highly irritating to the mediastinum and peritoneum; water-soluble contrast = less irritating and may be used if perf = poss
claims.quote: The main contraindication to a radiographic contrast studies is Suspected perforation Perforation is a contraindication because free barium is highly irritating to the mediastinum and peritoneum; water-soluble contrast is less irritating and may be used if perforation is possible.
claims.locator: Radiographs and Contrast Studies of the Abdomen

claims.text: High-resolution esophageal manometry = the preferred diagnostic test: incomplete LES relaxation w an ↑median integrated relaxation P and complete absence of peristalsis
claims.quote: High resolution esophageal manometry is the preferred diagnostic test for achalasia. This test shows incomplete relaxation of the LES with an elevated median integrated relaxation pressure in the supine or upright position and the complete absence of peristalsis (2).

claims.text: Manometric subtypes: type I (classic), swallowing results in ⍉Δ in esophageal P; type II, swallowing increases P in the entire esophagus; type III (spastic), swallowing often results in lumen-obliterating contractions
claims.quote: Subtypes of achalasia are (1): Type I achalasia (classic achalasia): Swallowing results in no change in esophageal pressure Type II achalasia: Swallowing increases pressure in the entire esophagus Type III achalasia (spastic achalasia): Swallowing often results in lumen-obliterating contractions

claims.text: Esophagoscopy: upstream esophageal dilate and chronic stasis chgs in the mucosa but ⍉obstructing lesion; the LES may be closed
claims.quote: Esophagoscopy is often performed. Findings include upstream esophageal dilation and chronic stasis changes in the mucosa but no obstructing lesion. The LES may be closed.

claims.text: Pseudoachalasia (similar Sx) may be ← CA @ the GE junction, diagnosed by CT of the chest and abd or by EUS w bx
claims.quote: Symptoms similar to those of achalasia (ie, pseudoachalasia) may be due to cancer at the gastroesophageal junction, which can be diagnosed by CT of the chest and abdomen or by endoscopic ultrasound with biopsy.

claims.text: Eti A neurogenic esophageal motility dx: impaired esophageal peristalsis and a lack of LES relaxation during swallowing
claims.quote: Achalasia is a neurogenic esophageal motility disorder characterized by impaired esophageal peristalsis and a lack of lower esophageal sphincter relaxation during swallowing.

claims.text: Thought to be caused by a loss of ganglion cells in the myenteric plexus (denerve of esophageal musc); the cause of the denerve = unknown, but viral and autoimmune Eti are sus; certain tumors may cause achalasia (direct obstruct or paraneoplastic); Chagas dz may also result in achalasia
claims.quote: It is thought to be caused by a loss of ganglion cells in the myenteric plexus of the esophagus, resulting in denervation of esophageal muscle. Etiology of the denervation is unknown, but viral and autoimmune causes are suspected, and certain tumors may cause achalasia either by direct obstruction or as a paraneoplastic process (1). Chagas disease, which causes destruction of autonomic ganglia, may also result in achalasia.

claims.text: Mech: ↑P @ the LES → obstruct w 2/2 dilate of the esophagus; retention of undigested food and liquid = common
claims.quote: Increased pressure at the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) causes obstruction with secondary dilation of the esophagus. Esophageal retention of undigested food and liquid is common.

claims.text: Sx Insidious onset, gradual progression over months or years; dysphagia for both solids and liquids = the major Sx; heartburn in up to ≈ 40%; nocturnal regurg of undigested food = common and may cause cough and pulm aspiration (aspiration PNA or, chronically, bronchiectasis); CP = less common
claims.quote: Onset is insidious, and progression is gradual over months or years. Dysphagia for both solids and liquids is the major symptom. Heartburn occurs in up to approximately 40% of patients (1, 2). Nocturnal regurgitation of undigested food is also common and may cause cough and pulmonary aspiration, leading to aspiration pneumonia or, chronically, bronchiectasis. Chest pain is less common but may occur with swallowing or spontaneously.

claims.text: Mild-mod wt loss; when wt loss = pronounced, particularly in older adults whose dysphagia developed rapidly, consider pseudoachalasia from a tumor of the GE junction
claims.quote: Mild to moderate weight loss occurs; when weight loss is pronounced, particularly in older adults whose symptoms of dysphagia developed rapidly, pseudoachalasia secondary to a tumor of the gastroesophageal junction should be considered.

claims.text: Incidence of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma = significantly ↑relative to the gen pop, although still ↓
claims.quote: Incidence of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in patients with achalasia is significantly increased relative to the general population, although incidence is still low (2, 3).

claims.text: Tx and next step ⍉therapy restores peristalsis; tx aims to reduce the P @ the LES and = ⍉curative
claims.quote: No therapy restores peristalsis; treatment of achalasia is aimed at reducing the pressure at the LES and is not curative (1).

claims.text: Effective first-line therapies: pneumatic balloon dilate of the LES, peroral endoscopic myotomy and laparoscopic Heller myotomy; these appear roughly equivalent for type I and II, while peroral endoscopic myotomy appears S. for type III
claims.quote: The American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy and the American College of Gastroenterology both recognize pneumatic balloon dilation of the LES, peroral endoscopic myotomy, and laparoscopic Heller myotomy as effective first-line therapies (1, 2). While these 3 therapies all appear roughly equivalent in efficacy for type I and type II achalasia, peroral endoscopic myotomy appears superior for type III achalasia.

claims.text: When surg myotomy = performed, fundoplication = also recommended to reduce reflux
claims.quote: When surgical myotomy is performed, fundoplication is also recommended to reduce reflux (1).

claims.text: ⍉a candidate for strd tx: endoscopic botulinum toxin type A inj into the LES may be tried; improvement USU occurs in 70 to 80% for the first mo and may last 6 months to over 1 yr
claims.quote: In patients who are not candidates for standard endoscopic or surgical treatment options, chemical denervation of cholinergic nerves in the distal esophagus by direct endoscopic injection of botulinum toxin type A into the LES may be tried. Clinical improvement usually occurs in 70 to 80% of patients for the first month (4) and may last 6 months to over 1 year.

claims.text: Nitrates or CCBs have been used but have ⍉been shown to be effective
claims.quote: Medications such as nitrates or calcium channel blockers have been used but have not been shown to be effective.
